title: Partner dependency unconfirmed with no alternative
thresholds_source: docs/decisions/risk-thresholds.md — D-M-RISK-3 + AI-1 (same record as the brownfield-dd twin; anchors are record-scoped, not procedure-scoped); activated by ADR-0060
notes: risk-thresholds.md AI-1 - exact twin of brownfield-dd's criterion of the same name: same evidence vars, same D-M-RISK-3 conjunction verbatim ('no alternative' = fewer than two active candidates: status in {contacted, in_negotiation, signed}; dependency = the max-severity aggregation reading high), and the same gd-0022-risk-thresholds anchors - anchors are record-scoped, not procedure-scoped, so the same record governs both procedures. Same evidence as the graded amber rule risk-dd-partner-sourcing per D-M-RISK-3's 'both, non-competing' boundary: the graded signal and this kill path each do their own job; the kill action is never weakened by the graded signal and never substitutes for it. Screening-stage semantics: the snapshot filler seeds risk.partner_candidates_active / risk.partner_dependency_risk only when a deal_structure_hypothesis exists, so before that point this criterion evaluates UNASSESSED and is listed in the unassessed set for the caller to decide - never a silent pass, never a defaulted halt. DMN documentation aid only (no runtime effect): hit policy: first-hit conjunction (A and B) → mark_conditional. Activated by ADR-0060 together with the db/lib/kill-criteria.ts evaluator: enabled=true with policy_id + thresholds_source satisfies the anti-tamper gate (registry check c), and the evaluator enforces the same gate at runtime.
evaluable_from_evidence: risk.partner_* <- partner_candidate (project scope); partner sourcing after the S4 route (Q3 = S5); project-scoped source; re-evaluated at fs, the first project gate (ADR-0193 §14.1)
